Theorem
[Boundedness of the inverse] ↗ thm:third-existence-spectrum ↗ thm:energy-estimates 1. ch6:6.2-thm-6\group Weak Solutions

If $\lambda otin \Sigma $, there exists a constant $C$ such that \[ (29) \qquad \| u\| _{L^2(U)} \leq C\| f\| _{L^2(U)}, \] whenever $f \in L^2(U)$ and $u \in H_0^1(U)$ is the unique weak solution of \[ egin{cases} Lu = \lambda u + f & ext{in } U \ u = 0 & ext{on } \partial U. \end{cases} \] The constant $C$ depends only on $\lambda $, $U$ and the coefficients of $L$.

No uniform choice of $C$ is possible as $\lambda $ approaches an eigenvalue.

Proof

\sketch If the estimate failed, normalize solutions with $\| u_k\| _{L^2}=1$ and right-hand sides tending to zero. Energy bounds and Rellich compactness yield a subsequence converging strongly in $L^2$ to a normalized homogeneous solution, contradicting $\lambda otin \Sigma $.

□
